A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Monitored MBIE-EB research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning simulations, learning curves, visitation analyses, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B and G.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation results, revised learning curves, visitation analyses, and retained ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B and C.

M1.justification: The two-instance MBIE-EB procedure, component-specific bonuses, pessimistic treatment of unobserved rewards, and observe/optimize scheduling remain. Explicit known-monitor equations and new pseudocode expand documentation without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same environments and monitor families, including stochastic observability, permanently hidden rewards, and known monitors. The 48 benchmarks highlighted in v2 Figure 6 already appear in v1 Appendix B.3 and Figure 9; coverage has not doubled.

E2.justification: Directed-E2 remains the principal comparator. The optimistic and pessimistic MBIE-EB variants and known-monitor comparison also appear in both versions, within corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Directed-E2's initial visitation values change from S0 = 0 in v1 Table 2 to Psi_init = 1 in v2 Appendix D.2. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not explain whether it corrects documentation or reflects reruns. Discounting, evaluation frequency, and test-episode counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Bottleneck visitation analysis in Figure 5 contains revised Directed-E2 trajectories, retaining the question of whether agents learn to avoid unobservable-reward states. The optimistic/pessimistic ablation plots themselves are unchanged between v1 Appendix G and v2 Appendix C; their expanded explanations do not constitute new tests.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 30 independent random seeds and 95% confidence intervals. Revised curve and interval values do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice or an increased run count.

E6.justification: Learning curves in Figure 4, Directed-E2 visitation curves in Figure 5, and several corresponding benchmark panels are revised. The principal rankings and reported 30% known-monitor benefit remain. These are updated results, not established same-setting performance gains, particularly given the revised baseline initialization.

T1.justification: v2 adds a trajectory-based indistinguishability definition in Appendix H and a bandit lower-bound corollary supporting a new claim of tight dependence on inverse observability in Appendix I. It also revises proof definitions and steps while retaining Theorem 3.1's upper bound. The new corollary's proof contains unjustified bounded-runtime and conditional-expectation steps.

C1.justification: The headline empirical claim expands from 22 wins among 24 benchmarks to 44 among 48, drawing on coverage already present in v1's appendix. The three principal contributions remain. Adding 'Truthful' to the title makes an existing assumption explicit rather than introducing a new restriction.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations in its expanded captions: Figure 10 suggests stronger inverse-observability dependence for Directed-E2, and Figure 11 connects known-monitor performance to robustness against monitor-space size. Ablation mechanisms receive fuller explanations, while the main limitations in Section 5 remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 supplies a repository link. v2 also documents zero-count handling, gives explicit known-monitor expressions, and adds pseudocode for both algorithms. Existing evaluation details, value-iteration budget, hardware, and runtime information are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references covering options, reward-uncertain MDPs, PAC analysis, and bandit lower bounds, including Machado and Bowling, Regan and Boutilier, and Mannor and Tsitsiklis. These broaden local context while retaining the central positioning relative to Mon-MDP research and MBIE-EB.

P1.justification: There is extensive editing across the abstract, preliminaries, method explanations, experimental narrative, and proofs. Terminology and notation are revised throughout, appendices are reorganized, and the previously terse ablation section gains a substantial explanatory narrative.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the miniature 24-panel main-text summary with the existing full 48-panel display, relocates Figure 5, and reorganizes the ablations into numbered Figures 12–13 with detailed captions. Hyperparameter tables are restructured, algorithm displays are added, and axes and captions receive further changes.

improvement.justification: Code-access information, pseudocode, expanded explanations, and reorganized figures improve usability. However, the new tightness claim relies on Corollary I.2's flawed printed proof: almost-sure termination does not imply a fixed finite runtime bound, and conditional expectations are combined without probability weights. These documentation gains and theoretical reliability problems leave the net overall quality change unclear.
